thread:
sara: Seeing repeated interface flaps and RX/TX errors on a subset of p4d nodes in us-west-2 GPU pool. East-west traffic to other serving nodes shows packet loss spikes and higher tail latency.
alex: Which metrics are you seeing? can you paste dmesg / ethtool -S for one of the affected nodes?
sara: Pasted below from node gpu-p4d-12
```
[ 12345.678901] mlx5_core 0000:86:00.0 enp134s0f0: NIC Link is Up
[ 12346.789012] mlx5_core 0000:86:00.0 enp134s0f0: NIC Link is Down
[ 12346.789015] mlx5_core 0000:86:00.0 enp134s0f0: firmware error MCQERR 0x4000000
[ 12346.789020] mlx5_core 0000:86:00.0 enp134s0f0: Resetting adapter
```
ethtool -S enp134s0f0 shows rx_errors: 1245 tx_errors: 630 rx_missed_errors: 0
```

alex: That pattern looks like an MLX driver/firmware mismatch. Which driver/fw versions are on the AMI?
sara: Kernel 6.1.18, mlx5_core 5.12.1, fw reported 12.26.1020 by ethtool -i
mike: We've seen similar on p3dn/p4d in another account when RDMA was enabled. Cloud provider had a firmware regression for fw < 12.48.x causing sporadic link resets under certain packet sizes.
laura: Quick mitigations: 1) cordon + drain affected nodes, 2) drop MTU from 9000 -> 1500 as a temporary step, 3) disable TSO/GSO on iface to reduce large-seg bursts. Commands:
```
sudo ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1500
sudo ethtool -K eth0 tso off gso off gro off
```
sara: Tried disabling TSO/GSO on one node — packet loss went down but throughput also dropped ~18%. So it's a trade-off. Still seeing occasional dmesg resets.
alex: We should treat this as a firmware-level bug. I'll open a support case with the cloud NIC vendor. In parallel, can we prepare an AMI with pinned kernel 5.15 + vendor-recommended mlx5 package? That was stable in our prior rollouts.
mike: Agree. Also add a canary group in staging with RDMA stress (ib_send_bw / ib_write_bw) to validate before mass rollout.
laura: I'll create the incident and schedule a rolling maintenance window. oncall-bot, create INC and notify finance for potential cost impact from using warm spares.
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-2357 created. Paging infra oncall. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/nic-flap>
sara: We've quarantined 12 nodes and redirected traffic to the warm spare GPUs; that increases our short-term GPU spend by ~8% for the region (estimate sent to finance).
mike: For long-term, we need automated detection: alert on ethX rx_errors > 100/min + dmesg mlx5_core resets -> auto-cordon. I'll add that to the SRE alerting playbook.
alex: Timeline: I can build and bake a 5.15 AMI with updated mlx5 driver and firmware utility today, roll to 3 canary nodes tonight, and start a gradual rollout if green. ETA first canary 02:00 UTC.
laura: Sounds good. I'll own the maintenance window and AWS support ticket. Keep updates in this thread and tag infra-oncall when we start migration.
sara: Thanks. Will attach node list and perf graphs to the incident. For now throttling east-west load balancing to avoid large packet bursts is helping.
mike: FYI — if vendor pushes a firmware image we may need console reboot rather than ami-level change. Plan both paths.
laura: :thumbsup: schedule confirmed 02:00-05:00 UTC. Notify customers if SLA impacted >1%.
alex: I'll post the post-mortem template link after the rollout. +1 for adding automated cordon on repeated mlx5 resets.
sara: Updating incident with latest logs. ping me for any quick rollbacks."
